newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge Ontario union strikes - report.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge Ontario union strikes - report.

text.p: Falconbridge Ltd's 1,400 unionized workers at its Sudbury, Ontario operations went on strike on Friday, the Canadian Press news agency said.
Falconbridge spokeswoman Caroline Casselman said she had received media calls for reaction to the walkout, but that she had no direct confirmation of the strike.
Union officials could not be reached for comment.
The Canadian Auto Workers union, which represents the unionized workers, had set a strike deadline of 0800 EDT/1200 GMT today. Falconbridge is Canada's second biggest nickel producer.
The Falconbridge spokesman in Sudbury, Brian McLeod, said that workers were picketing the Sudbury operations.
Falconbridge's Sudbury operations last produced 45,700 tonnes of nickel, 50,000 tonnes of copper and 1,600 tonnes of cobalt, including custom feed.
A mining analyst has said that the strike would have to last a long time before it made a significant impact on metals markets.
Another analyst said Falconbridge likely had sufficient inventories to meet customer demands during a short union shutdown.
The mine workers voted 91.28 perent in favor of a strike mandate in July.
